requirements.name: Backup plan min frequency and min retention check
requirements.reason: Same pinned Steampipe control in every benchmark. Its text (AWS Config backup-plan-min-frequency-and-min-retention-check) requires at least one rule meeting frequency and 35-day retention: aws_nist_backup_plan_min_retention_35_days with an operator-declared frequency (UNKNOWN without it). The pinned query is retention-only per rule, kept as aws.c2b.backup.plan_rules_retention_35; neither alone completes the row, so it stays PARTIAL.
evidence: steampipe-mod-aws-compliance@803dda1f conformance_pack/backup.pp:31-34 control text; :158-182 retention-only query

new_checks.data_source: existing collected backup_plan GetBackupPlan detail: Plan.BackupPlan.Rules[].ScheduleExpression, ScheduleExpressionTimezone, EnableContinuousBackup and Lifecycle; plus the operator-declared, scope-bound required_frequency_hours sealed in snapshot metadata.compliance_policy.aws_backup_plan (operator policy input, not an observed cloud fact; never defaulted)
new_checks.predicate: Per collected backup plan in its audited account/Region: PASS when at least one rule has a cron schedule on a fixed UTC offset whose exact maximum gap over the 400-year Gregorian cycle is at most the operator required_frequency_hours and keeps recovery points at least 35 days (Lifecycle.DeleteAfterDays >= 35 or no expiry); FAIL when every rule is proven to miss the frequency or the retention, or the plan has no rules; UNKNOWN when no rule is proven to qualify and any rule cannot be bounded (rate(), L/W/#, wrapping or year-limited cron, DST or rule-changing time zone, event-based deletion, continuous-backup coverage, denied or malformed facts), or when the operator frequency policy is missing, malformed or does not cover the scope. Configured coverage only, not observed recovery points or job success.
new_checks.title: Backup plan min frequency and min retention check
new_checks.description: Detects an AWS Backup plan in which no rule both runs at least as often as the operator-approved interval and keeps recovery points for at least 35 days, so the plan cannot meet the backup frequency and 35-day retention objective by configuration.
new_checks.remediation_hint: Add or edit a rule in the AWS Backup plan so its schedule creates recovery points at least as often as the approved interval and its lifecycle keeps them 35 days or longer, and declare that interval as scan policy.

evidence: steampipe-mod-aws-compliance@803dda1f conformance_pack/backup.pp:31-34 control text; :158-182 retention-only query

new_checks.data_source: existing collected backup_plan GetBackupPlan detail: Plan.BackupPlan.Rules[].ScheduleExpression, ScheduleExpressionTimezone, EnableContinuousBackup and Lifecycle; plus the operator-declared, scope-bound required_frequency_hours sealed in snapshot metadata.compliance_policy.aws_backup_plan (operator policy input, not an observed cloud fact; never defaulted)
new_checks.predicate: Per collected backup plan in its audited account/Region: PASS when at least one rule has a cron schedule on a fixed UTC offset whose exact maximum gap over the 400-year Gregorian cycle is at most the operator required_frequency_hours and keeps recovery points at least 35 days (Lifecycle.DeleteAfterDays >= 35 or no expiry); FAIL when every rule is proven to miss the frequency or the retention, or the plan has no rules; UNKNOWN when no rule is proven to qualify and any rule cannot be bounded (rate(), L/W/#, wrapping or year-limited cron, DST or rule-changing time zone, event-based deletion, continuous-backup coverage, denied or malformed facts), or when the operator frequency policy is missing, malformed or does not cover the scope. Configured coverage only, not observed recovery points or job success.

The evaluator tests RDS instance storage encryption is enabled (fields: PubliclyAccessible, Versioning), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: RDS DB snapshots should be encrypted at rest
requirements.reason: Ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) snapshots. The evaluator tests DB cluster snapshot is encrypted (all engines) (fields: DBClusterSnapshotArn, StorageEncrypted, DBSnapshotArn); DB instance snapshot is encrypted (fields: DBSnapshotArn, Encrypted), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift clusters should be encrypted with KMS
requirements.reason: Ensure that AWS Redshift clusters are using a specified AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for encryption. The evaluator tests Redshift cluster is encrypted with a declared KMS key (fields: Encrypted, KmsKeyId), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: S3 bucket default encryption should be enabled
requirements.reason: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets. The evaluator tests S3 bucket has native default encryption configuration (fields: Encryption, ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration.Rules, ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.SSEAlgorithm), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: S3 bucket default encryption should be enabled with KMS
requirements.reason: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets. The evaluator tests S3 bucket default encryption names a KMS key (fields: ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.SSEAlgorithm, ReplicationConfiguration.Rules), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: SageMaker endpoint configuration encryption should be enabled
requirements.reason: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) is enabled for your SageMaker endpoint. The evaluator tests SageMaker endpoint configuration declares a KMS key (fields: ProductionVariants), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: SageMaker notebook instance encryption should be enabled
requirements.reason: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) is enabled for your SageMaker notebook. The evaluator tests SageMaker notebook instance storage uses a KMS key, using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: Secrets Manager secrets should be encrypted using CMK
requirements.reason: Ensure that all secrets in AWS Secrets Manager are encrypted using the AWS managed key (aws/secretsmanager) or a customer managed key that was created in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The evaluator tests Secret is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key (fields: CreatedDate), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: SNS topics should be encrypted at rest
requirements.reason: To help protect data at rest, ensure that your AWS Simple Notification Service (AWS SNS) topics require encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The evaluator tests SNS topic declares KMS encryption (fields: Engine, CopyTagsToSnapshot, EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: IAM user access keys should be rotated at least every 90 days
requirements.reason: The credentials are audited for authorized devices, users, and processes by ensuring IAM access keys are rotated as per organizational policy. The evaluator tests Active IAM access key is newer than the captured 90-day date cutoff (fields: Status), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: IAM password policies for users should have strong configurations
requirements.reason: The identities and the credentials are issued, managed, and verified based on an organizational IAM password policy. The evaluator tests Account password policy enforces strong min length 14 reuse 24 age 90, using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: IAM root user hardware MFA should be enabled
requirements.reason: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring hardware MFA is enabled for the root user. The evaluator tests Root MFA is enabled without an assigned virtual MFA device (fields: SummaryMap.AccountMFAEnabled, SerialNumber, User.Arn), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: IAM root user MFA should be enabled
requirements.reason: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring MFA is enabled for the root user. The evaluator tests Root account MFA is configured (fields: SummaryMap.AccountMFAEnabled, SummaryMap.AccountAccessKeysPresent), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: IAM users with console access should have MFA enabled
requirements.reason: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that MFA is enabled for all AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users that have a console password. The evaluator tests Credential-report password-enabled principals have MFA, using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: DynamoDB tables should be in a backup plan
requirements.reason: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS DynamoDB tables are a part of an AWS Backup plan. The evaluator tests DynamoDB table is in a backup selection by ARN or tag key (fields: TableArn, Resources, ListOfTags), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: DynamoDB table should be protected by backup plan
requirements.reason: Ensure that AWS DynamoDB tables are protected by a backup plan. The evaluator tests DynamoDB table is an AWS Backup protected resource (fields: TableArn, ResourceArn, ResourceType), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: EBS volumes should be in a backup plan
requirements.reason: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes are a part of an AWS Backup plan. The evaluator tests EBS volume is selected by an AWS Backup plan (ARN or tag key) (fields: VolumeId, Resources, ListOfTags), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: EBS volumes should be protected by a backup plan
requirements.reason: Ensure that AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes are protected by a backup plan. The evaluator tests EBS volume is an AWS Backup protected resource (fields: VolumeId, Resources, ListOfTags), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should be protected by backup plan
requirements.reason: Ensure that AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances are protected by a backup plan. The evaluator tests EC2 instance is an AWS Backup protected resource (fields: InstanceId, GroupName, SecurityGroups), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: EFS file systems should be in a backup plan
requirements.reason: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Elastic File System (AWS EFS) file systems are a part of an AWS Backup plan. The evaluator tests EFS file system automatic backups are enabled (fields: false), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: EFS file systems should be protected by backup plan
requirements.reason: Ensure that AWS Elastic File System (AWS EFS) File Systems are protected by a backup plan. The evaluator tests EFS file system is an AWS Backup protected resource (fields: FileSystemArn, ResourceArn, ResourceType), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: ElastiCache Redis cluster automatic backup should be enabled with retention period of 15 days or greater
requirements.reason: When automatic backups are enabled, AWS ElastiCache creates a backup of the cluster on a daily basis. The evaluator tests ElastiCache replication group retains snapshots at least 15 days (fields: ReplicationGroupId, EngineVersion), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: FSx file system should be protected by backup plan
requirements.reason: Checks if AWS FSx File Systems are protected by a backup plan. The evaluator tests FSx file system is a protected resource in AWS Backup (fields: ResourceARN, ResourceArn, ResourceType), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: Neptune DB clusters should have automated backups enabled
requirements.reason: This control checks whether a Neptune DB cluster has automated backups enabled, and a backup retention period greater than or equal to 7 days. The evaluator tests Neptune cluster retains automated backups at least 7 days (fields: BackupRetentionPeriod), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: RDS Aurora clusters should be protected by backup plan
requirements.reason: Checks if AWS Aurora DB clusters are protected by a backup plan. The evaluator tests Aurora cluster is an AWS Backup protected resource (fields: Engine, DBClusterArn, ResourceArn), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance backup should be enabled
requirements.reason: The backup feature of AWS RDS creates backups of your databases and transaction logs. The evaluator tests RDS instance automated backup retention is at least one day (fields: BackupRetentionPeriod, CopyTagsToSnapshot, IAMDatabaseAuthenticationEnabled), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: RDS DB instances should be in a backup plan
requirements.reason: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are a part of an AWS Backup plan. The evaluator tests RDS instance is in a backup selection by ARN or tag key (fields: DBInstanceArn, Key, Selections), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance should be protected by backup plan
requirements.reason: Ensure that AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are protected by a backup plan. The evaluator tests RDS instance is an AWS Backup protected resource (fields: DBInstanceArn, ResourceArn, ResourceType), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift clusters should have automatic snapshots enabled
requirements.reason: This control checks whether AWS Redshift clusters have automated snapshots enabled. The evaluator tests Redshift automated snapshot retention is at least 7 days (fields: AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod, AllowVersionUpgrade, Encrypted), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: CloudFront distributions should have origin access identity enabled
requirements.reason: This control checks whether an AWS CloudFront distribution with AWS S3 Origin type has Origin Access Identity (OAI) configured. The evaluator tests CloudFront s3.amazonaws.com origins declare an origin access identity (fields: DomainName, OriginAccessIdentity, Id), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: S3 bucket object lock should be enabled
requirements.reason: Ensure that your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) bucket has lock enabled, by default. The evaluator tests S3 bucket has an Object Lock configuration (fields: ObjectLockConfiguration, Notifications), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: S3 bucket versioning should be enabled
requirements.reason: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) bucket versioning helps keep multiple variants of an object in the same AWS S3 bucket. The evaluator tests S3 bucket versioning is enabled (fields: Versioning, Logging, Acl.Grants), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: AWS Config should be enabled
requirements.reason: This control checks whether AWS Config is enabled in the account for the local Region and is recording all resources. The evaluator tests An AWS Config recorder is recording without a reported failure in the selected region (fields: name, Status.ConfigurationRecordersStatus, recording), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: Elasticsearch domain should send logs to CloudWatch
requirements.reason: Ensure that AWS OpenSearch Service (OpenSearch Service) domains are configured to send logs to AWS CloudWatch Logs. The evaluator tests Elasticsearch domain publishes error, search slow and index slow logs to CloudWatch (fields: DomainEndpointOptions.TLSSecurityPolicy), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: OpenSearch domains should have audit logging enabled.
requirements.reason: This control checks whether OpenSearch service domains have audit logging enabled. The evaluator tests OpenSearch domain publishes audit logs, using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: OpenSearch domains logs to AWS CloudWatch Logs
requirements.reason: This control checks whether AWS OpenSearch Service domains are configured to send logs to CloudWatch logs. The evaluator tests OpenSearch domain enabled log types each target a CloudWatch log group, using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: ECR repositories should have image scan on push enabled
requirements.reason: Ensure AWS Elastic Container Registry (ECR) repositories have image scanning enabled. The evaluator tests ECR repository has scan-on-push or a matching enhanced scanning rule (fields: imageScanningConfiguration.scanOnPush, repositoryName, scanningConfiguration), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: GuardDuty should be enabled
requirements.reason: AWS GuardDuty can help to monitor and detect potential cybersecurity events by using threat intelligence feeds. The evaluator tests GuardDuty is enabled in the selected region (fields: Configuration.Status, name, Status.ConfigurationRecordersStatus), using the resource's collected configuration fields.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should not have a public IP address
requirements.reason: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances cannot be publicly accessed. The evaluator tests EC2 instance has no public IPv4 address, using the resource's collected configuration fields.
